scams.name: La Mère Poulard Restaurant Price Trap
scams.description: La Mère Poulard trades on a century of hype for its signature soufflé omelette. Visitors report paying €40–€80 for a basic omelette — often dry, flavorless, and ‘nothing extraordinary.’ A bottle of cider here runs €19–€26, versus under €3 at any supermarket on the mainland. Service is notoriously slow; 30–40 minutes just to get your order taken is typical.
scams.avoidance: Skip dining on the island entirely. If you must eat on-island, check menu prices carefully before sitting. Eat at restaurants in nearby Pontorson or Cancale instead. Bring a picnic lunch to the island.
scams.location: La Mère Poulard restaurant, L’Auberge de La Mère Poulard, La Mère Poulard Cafe, Grande Rue

scams.name: Island Restaurant Tourist Trap
scams.description: Every restaurant on the island gets described as a tourist trap — bad service, mediocre food, prices that nobody who lives nearby would pay. With no repeat customers, the restaurants have no incentive to improve. Visitors report €4.50 for a 500 ml bottle of water, €9.80 for a small beer, €7 per glass of wine, and €3.50 for a mediocre crêpe.
scams.avoidance: Pack your own food and water before arriving. Eat breakfast before visiting and dinner after leaving. Coffee or aperitifs are acceptable for the experience, but avoid full meals. Visit the fishing port of Cancale nearby for excellent seafood at fair prices.
scams.location: Grande Rue restaurants, all restaurants on Mont-Saint-Michel island

scams.name: Overpriced Parking Lot
scams.description: The official parking lot charges inflated prices, with little signage about the cost before you drive in. Visitors report paying €14–€25, including €17 for just 30 minutes in one case and €9.80 for under two hours in a nearly empty lot in another. Once you’ve driven to Mont-Saint-Michel, there is no alternative — and the pricing reflects that.
scams.avoidance: Check current parking rates online before visiting. Budget 15-20 euros for parking in your trip costs. Consider taking public transport or organized tours instead. Arrive early or late to minimize parking time.
scams.location: Official Mont-Saint-Michel parking area, P1 main parking lot

scams.name: Unlicensed Bay Crossing Danger
scams.description: The bay around Mont-Saint-Michel contains deadly quicksand pockets and experiences extreme tides that rise at speeds up to 6 km/hour — faster than a person can run. Tourists attempting to cross the bay without certified guides have died or required helicopter rescue after becoming trapped in quicksand as tides rushed in. In 2019 alone, multiple rescues were needed including one helicopter extraction.
scams.avoidance: Do not set foot on the bay without a certified guide from the Préfecture de la Manche — people have died. Book official bay-crossing tours through the tourism office. Check tide schedules before you visit. There are only 67 officially authorized guides; verify credentials before paying.
scams.location: Mont-Saint-Michel Bay, tidal flats around the island, areas between parking and island

scams.name: Worthless Museum Trap
scams.description: Mont-Saint-Michel has several small private museums charging €9 each or €18 for a multi-museum pass. Visitors describe them as dusty and dilapidated, with shabby exhibits crammed into tiny rooms. Three of the four have been called ‘a disgrace,’ with dirt, mold on the walls, and little historical content. They exist to separate tourists from their money.
scams.avoidance: Skip all private museums on the island. The only worthwhile paid attraction is the Abbey itself (13 euros). Read reviews before paying any entrance fee. The free walking experience and architecture are the real attractions.
scams.location: Musee Historique, small museums on Grande Rue, museum complex on the island

scams.name: Candy Shop Overcharging
scams.description: Several candy shops on the Grande Rue use deceptive pricing. Prices are listed at €8 per 100 grams — roughly double the typical tourist rate of €4. Visitors report paying as much as €31 for a single bag of sweets. Some shops use aggressive sales tactics, pressuring you to pay after you’ve already filled the bag.
scams.avoidance: Ask for total price before filling any bag. Calculate the per-gram cost before selecting items. Don’t feel obligated to buy if prices seem excessive. Buy sweets in mainland towns instead.
scams.location: Candy shops on Grande Rue, sweet shops along main street

scams.name: Crowded Street Theft
scams.description: Mont-Saint-Michel’s single narrow street becomes extremely congested, especially from 10:30am to 5pm in peak season. The crushing crowds create ideal conditions for pickpockets who exploit tourists distracted by sights and jostled by crowds. Items left unattended — including wheelchairs, strollers, and bags at the abbey entrance where they must be left — can easily be stolen.
scams.avoidance: Visit early morning (before 10am) or evening (after 5pm) to avoid worst crowds. Wear crossbody bags in front of your body. Keep valuables in front pockets or money belt. Never leave bags unattended even briefly.
scams.location: Grande Rue (main street), narrow passages, Abbey entrance area, shuttle bus queues

scams.name: Parking Lot Vehicle Break-In
scams.description: Thieves target vehicles in the Mont-Saint-Michel parking lot, particularly rental cars identifiable by stickers or foreign plates. They watch tourists rearrange luggage in the lot (revealing valuables), then break into cars while owners spend hours visiting the island. This is part of a wider pattern of tourist parking lot thefts across Normandy.
scams.avoidance: Move valuables to the trunk before you arrive, not in the lot where thieves are watching. Don’t rearrange luggage visibly in the parking area. Peel off rental company stickers before you leave the airport. Park in high-traffic areas near the entrance rather than the quieter edges.
scams.location: Mont-Saint-Michel parking lot, remote sections of parking area

scams.name: Hotel Overbooking Scam
scams.description: Hotels on Mont-Saint-Michel (mostly owned by one family/company with monopoly pricing power) have been reported to overbook rooms and then relocate guests to inferior mainland hotels at the last minute. Visitors receive emails about ‘overbooking’ and forced relocation to distant hotels at the same premium price, suspecting they were bumped for higher-paying tour groups.
scams.avoidance: Book well in advance and get written confirmation. Consider staying in mainland hotels intentionally — they offer better value. Book directly with hotels rather than through aggregators. Have backup accommodation options researched.
scams.location: Hotels on Mont-Saint-Michel island, L’Auberge Saint Pierre, Poulard Group hotels

scams.name: Tide Timing Trap
scams.description: Tourists often plan visits around seeing spectacular high tides but don’t understand tide mechanics. High tides reaching 14 meters can occur, but they don’t happen every day. Conversely, those who don’t check tide schedules may be caught off-guard by rapidly rising water on the causeway or bay areas. The incoming tide can isolate visitors or trap them against walls.
scams.avoidance: Check tide schedules online before visiting (available on tourism website). Understand that exceptional tides only occur a few times yearly. Time your visit for 2 hours before high tide for best experience. Never walk the bay without awareness of tide timing.
scams.location: Causeway to Mont-Saint-Michel, bay surrounding the island, lower ramparts
